sections.h2: Where is Alleghany County, Virginia, and what is inside it?
sections.html:
Alleghany County sits on the far western edge of Virginia, in the northernmost part of the Roanoke Region. The Allegheny Mountains run along its western side and gave the county its name, and the whole county lies in the Valley and Ridge part of the state.

It covers 449.7 square miles, and only about 0.7 percent of that is water. The Cowpasture and Jackson Rivers cross the county and come together just south of the boundary near Iron Gate to form the James River. The 2020 census counted 15,223 residents.

The county seat, Covington, is an independent city and is not part of the county. That matters to a seller, because a house with a Covington address can be billed by the city and not by Alleghany County. The largest town inside the county is Clifton Forge, which became a town again on July 1, 2001. Iron Gate and Low Moor are the other communities most often named.

sections.h2: What shaped the local economy and housing stock?
sections.html:
Paper and rail have carried Alleghany County's economy for a long time. WestRock runs a paperboard mill in Covington, described as the second largest on the East Coast, and an extrusion and converting plant in Low Moor. CSX Transportation operates a major locomotive fueling facility in Clifton Forge.

The county's early cash crop was hemp, and farmers later moved to grain, hay and livestock. Iron for the CSS Virginia came from Longdale Furnace in the county during the Civil War. Many present-day residents commute to Lewisburg, West Virginia, to Lexington or to Roanoke.

For a seller, the practical point is that the local job base is small and tied to a few large employers, so the pool of local buyers is limited. A buyer paying cash can take a house as it stands, which some owners prefer to waiting on a financed buyer.

sections.h2: How do roads and rail affect selling a house in Alleghany County?
sections.html:
Interstate 64 crosses the county east to west and U.S. Route 220 runs north to south. Amtrak's Cardinal serves the Clifton Forge station, about 12 miles from Covington.

Because many residents commute to Lewisburg, Lexington or Roanoke, access to the interstate is part of what any buyer considers. Describe your road access plainly when you talk to a buyer.

sections.h2: Who handles real estate tax in Alleghany County?
sections.html:
In Virginia the commissioner of the revenue oversees assessment, and the treasurer collects the bill. Localities may reassess on cycles from one to six years, and the commissioner supervises the work, according to Virginia Cooperative Extension.

Assessments are normally set as of January 1, and an owner who disagrees can go to the local board of equalization. The Alleghany County complex is at 9212 Winterberry Avenue in Covington, which is also the address the town of Clifton Forge lists for written appeals.

We could not open an Alleghany County page that states the current tax rate, the due dates or the late penalty, so we are not repeating figures for them here. The county treasurer and commissioner of the revenue can give you the current bill, the due date and what you owe through the closing date.

sections.h2: How does the Alleghany County Board of Equalization work?
sections.html:
The Board of Equalization hears assessment complaints and can raise, lower or leave an assessment unchanged. The Town of Clifton Forge posted the board's 2025 schedule, with hearings on five days in March 2025 from 9:00 am to 3:00 pm in the Board Room of the county complex.

  • Book a 15 minute slot by calling (540) 863-6640 between 8 am and 5 pm on weekdays, holidays excluded.
  • Or send a written complaint to 9212 Winterberry Avenue, Suite E, Covington, VA 24426.
  • Or appear at the hearing in person, with spoken remarks or written material.

The owner or agent starts with a presumption that the assessment is right. To overcome it, you must show that the assessment is not uniform with similar properties and back that with substantial evidence, or that the property is assessed above its fair market value. Those hearing dates are from 2025, so ask the county for the schedule that applies to the current notice.

sections.h2: What can you do if the board denies your appeal?
sections.html:
You can go to the circuit court. Virginia Code section 58.1-3984 lets an aggrieved owner apply to the circuit court of the locality, and the filing window is the later of three years after the end of the tax year or one year after the assessment date, with other cases listed in the statute.

For real property the assessor's value, or the value the board set, is presumed correct, and the owner has to rebut it by a preponderance of the evidence. Most owners who are about to sell do not pursue a court case, since the sale itself sets the number a buyer will pay.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid property tax when you sell in Alleghany County?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax follows the house, not the seller. Virginia Code section 58.1-3340 gives real estate a lien for taxes that ranks ahead of other liens, and it stays until the tax is paid to the taxing authority.

At a sale, the proceeds are applied to the taxes on the property. Who bears the current year's share is a matter of the contract, so the purchase agreement should state it. A title company or settlement attorney normally asks the treasurer for a payoff figure before closing.

  • Ask the treasurer for the balance through your expected closing date.
  • Pay the oldest delinquent bill first if more than one is open.
  • Keep the receipt, because the title company may ask to see it.

sections.h2: How much do penalties and transfer taxes cost in Virginia?
sections.html:
State law caps what a locality can charge. Under section 58.1-3916 the penalty for late payment cannot exceed 10 percent of the tax past due or $10, whichever is greater, and interest may not exceed 10 percent a year. Each locality sets its own terms by ordinance, so the Alleghany County figure may be lower than the cap.

Two transfer taxes show up on a deed. Under section 58.1-802 the grantor tax is 50 cents for each $500 of consideration, paid by the seller unless the parties agree otherwise. Under section 58.1-801 the state recordation tax is 25 cents per $100, and the statute does not say who pays. Local add-ons were not confirmed, so ask the circuit court clerk for the full recording cost.

sections.h2: What do owners in Alleghany County usually face when selling?
sections.html:
Owners selling here can run into a short list of problems.

  • Real estate tax that fell behind on a house that sits empty.
  • Repairs the owner cannot afford before listing.
  • A small local buyer pool, given the size of the county.
  • Uncertainty about whether the address is billed by the county or by the city of Covington.

If any of this describes your house, we can look at it as it is and give you a written cash offer, with no repairs on your side. Call or text and tell us the address.

faqs.q: Is Covington part of Alleghany County?
faqs.a: No. Covington is the county seat but it is an independent city and not part of the county, so a house inside the city limits is handled by the city. Check your bill to see which office sends it.

faqs.q: What is the largest town in Alleghany County?
faqs.a: Clifton Forge is the largest town. It reincorporated as a town within the county on July 1, 2001.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Alleghany County assessment?
faqs.a: Contact the county Board of Equalization. The town of Clifton Forge lists (540) 863-6640 for appointments and 9212 Winterberry Avenue, Suite E, Covington, for written complaints. You must show the assessment is above market value or not uniform with similar properties.

faqs.q: Can a buyer take over a house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes, but the tax must be dealt with at closing. Virginia gives the tax lien priority over other liens, so the unpaid amount is normally paid from the sale proceeds.

faqs.q: What is the most a Virginia locality can charge for a late real estate tax payment?
faqs.a: State law caps the penalty at 10 percent of the tax past due or $10, whichever is greater, and interest at 10 percent a year. The local ordinance sets the actual terms.
